questions.question: Which feature of Amazon Cognito supports identity federation among social and enterprise identity providers?
options: Requires manual integration with identity providers
Requires users to manage authentication infrastructure
Only supports user authentication through EC2
Does not support mobile or web applications
Offers integration with social and enterprise identity providers
questions.explanation: Amazon Cognito supports identity federation by serving as a central hub that natively integrates with public social providers (like Google, Facebook, Apple, and Amazon) as well as enterprise systems via SAML 2.0 or OpenID Connect (OIDC).

questions.question: What is one use case of AWS Resource Groups?
options: Creating resource groups based on tags or CloudFormation stacks
questions.explanation: AWS Resource Groups allows you to organize and manage your AWS resources collectively by creating dynamic groups based on shared tags or specific CloudFormation stacks.

questions.question: How does envelope encryption improve the scalability of AWS encryption practices?
options: By using TLS 1.3 instead of TLS 1.2 for all network traffic
By encrypting data keys under a CMK instead of encrypting large data directly
By encrypting each object with a unique AWS-managed key
By encrypting data directly with the customer master key (CMK)
questions.explanation: Envelope encryption uses a local data key to encrypt large data payloads, while the data key itself is encrypted under a root KMS Customer Master Key (CMK). This prevents network bottlenecks and bypasses the strict 4 KB direct payload limits of KMS.

questions.question: Which action can you perform when managing packages in AWS CodeArtifact?
options: Enable version control on the file system hosting the repository
Modify package source code directly in the repository
View, delete, and control access to individual package versions
Use EC2 to build and compile all packages
questions.explanation: AWS CodeArtifact provides built-in repository interfaces and APIs to view package metadata, delete old iterations, and apply IAM rules to restrict or authorize package usage across your development pipeline.

questions.question: Which feature(s) must be enabled to allow automatic patching in your AWS Elastic Beanstalk environment? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Managed Updates handles the automation engine for patches, but Elastic Beanstalk strictly mandates that Enhanced Health Monitoring must also be enabled to evaluate rolling health in real-time.

questions.question: Which two options are available for deploying .NET applications to AWS Elastic Beanstalk? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Elastic Beanstalk natively supports cross-platform modern workloads using .NET Core on Linux (Amazon Linux) alongside enterprise or legacy ecosystems running standard .NET on Windows Server IIS.

questions.question: What EC2 networking feature allows you to attach multiple IP addresses and security groups to a single instance?
questions.explanation: An Elastic Network Interface (ENI) functions as a virtual network card. You can map multiple private/public IPs and bind distinct combinations of Security Groups directly to an ENI.

questions.question: After copying WordPress files into /var/www/html, what change must be made in Apache's configuration to enable WordPress permalinks?
options: Replace the default index page with index.php
Change AllowOverride None to AllowOverride All in the /var/www/html directory block
questions.explanation: Changing AllowOverride to 'All' permits Apache to read and enforce localized URL routing rules contained within the WordPress .htaccess file.

questions.question: Which AWS CodeCommit capability includes fast-forward, squash, or three-way?
questions.explanation: Fast-forward, squash, and three-way define the standard merge actions available to combine divergent developer branches into target branches within CodeCommit.

questions.question: Which resource layer includes IOPS, throughput, and encryption as key parameters?
questions.explanation: IOPS, operational throughput metrics, and cryptographic rest-encryption represent core settings used to provision and evaluate block or object storage platforms like Amazon EBS and S3.

questions.question: While adding resources using AWS Resource Explorer, which type of properties can be filtered? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: AWS Resource Explorer supports distinct query prefix syntaxes to isolate infrastructure footprints, filtering directly by resource type, parent service, target account IDs, and linked applications.

questions.question: You are running 'sam deploy --guided' to deploy a new application. Which is the default name of the SAM configuration file?
questions.explanation: The guided deployment parameters captured by the AWS SAM CLI wizard automatically populate inside a structural configuration file named samconfig.toml by default.

questions.question: Which AWS monitoring service allows users to audit AWS resource usage?
questions.explanation: AWS CloudTrail tracks and logs the comprehensive history of account operations and API calls across the entire infrastructure footprint, serving as the central governance auditing register.

questions.question: Which architectural component of AMP is responsible for collecting performance data?
questions.explanation: The Prometheus Server (or an equivalent configured scraper agent) discovers workloads and harvests time-series metrics before forwarding them to the Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus workspace.

questions.question: How are metrics from a newly created EC2 instance sent to AWS CloudWatch?
options: By manually setting up an EC2 to CloudWatch connection via SSH
By installing a CloudWatch agent on the EC2 instance
EC2 metrics are not sent to CloudWatch
questions.explanation: Hypervisor-level baseline telemetry (such as CPU, basic network I/O, and disk operations) routes automatically to CloudWatch by default without server-side agent plugins or installations.

questions.question: How is the AWS Systems Manager agent installed on an EC2 instance running Amazon Linux 2?
options: The agent is deployed from the AWS Systems Manager Agent Deployment console
The AWS Systems Manager agent cannot be deployed on Amazon Linux 2
The AWS Systems Manager agent is installed by default on Amazon Linux 2
The agent configuration file is transferred to AWS Systems Manager via FTP
questions.explanation: The Systems Manager (SSM) Agent comes baked into the standard Amazon Linux 2 operating system image by default. It activates automatically when granted an appropriate IAM role.

questions.question: What is the primary distinction between Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling and AWS Application Auto Scaling?
options: EC2 scales endpoints while Application Auto Scaling scales clusters and AZs
Both EC2 and Application Auto Scaling do the same thing with different names
EC2 scales EC2 and DynamoDB while Application Auto Scaling scales only serverless
EC2 scales EC2 only while Application Auto Scaling covers many AWS services
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling handles virtual machine fleet adjustments exclusively, whereas Application Auto Scaling provides a standardized platform scaling interface for ECS, DynamoDB, and other native AWS platforms.

questions.question: Which AWS resources are supported by AWS Compute Optimizer?
options: AWS Lambda functions with memory and runtime tuning
Amazon S3 buckets with lifecycle and storage tiering
Amazon CloudFront distributions with caching optimization
Auto Scaling groups with scaling pattern analysis
EC2 instances with CPU, memory, and network analysis
questions.explanation: AWS Compute Optimizer leverages machine learning to review compute profiles and resources, supporting standalone EC2 instances, Auto Scaling configurations, Lambda allocations, and EBS volumes.

questions.question: You are creating an auto scaling group from an EC2 launch template. In step 4, 'Configure group size and scaling policies', which are options provided under Automatic scaling - optional?
questions.explanation: The AWS creation process provides options to keep capacity static using 'No scaling policies' or to leverage automated elasticity adjustments using 'Target tracking scaling policies'.

questions.question: You are configuring a CloudFront distribution. In Step 2, Specify origin, which Origin types are available to choose from?
questions.explanation: CloudFront features built-in delivery routing structures for S3 storage targets, API Gateway wrappers, and secure VPC internal endpoints using native VPC origins.

questions.question: Which is the most likely reason a load balancer marks healthy instances as unhealthy during peak traffic periods?
options: Listener ports are misconfigured for HTTPS traffic
Backend instances are not registered with the target group
Health check thresholds are too high to detect failures
Health check intervals and timeouts are too short for the applicationâ€™s response time
questions.explanation: Heavy traffic causes execution delays on hosting layers. Tight timeout margins cause healthy but slow systems to miss their deadlines, leading the balancer to report false errors.

questions.question: Which is the most likely cause of an application suddenly receiving 'Access Denied' errors when writing to an S3 bucket?
options: The storage class was changed to Glacier
The IAM or bucket policy was recently misconfigured
The storage capacity limit was exceeded
questions.explanation: HTTP 403 access issues denote authorization configuration breakdowns. This occurs from recent, faulty adjustments to identity access permissions or bucket safety policies.

questions.question: What is the likely cause when an application shows SSL/TLS handshake failures despite network connectivity being functional?
options: The IAM role attached to the instance lacks read permissions for S3
The SSL/TLS certificate is expired, missing, or does not match the hostname
The route table is misconfigured and missing a NAT gateway
The security group rules are blocking outbound traffic to port 443
questions.explanation: Handshake errors indicate that network paths are open, but cryptographic validation has failed. This is typically due to out-of-date, mismatched, or broken security certificate assets.

questions.question: What is a likely explanation for a spike in alerts from Shodan or other scanning tools targeting your cloud environment?
options: IAM permissions were overly restrictive for the user group
An internal endpoint was unintentionally made public
A load balancer was attached to the wrong availability zone
A CloudTrail misconfiguration exposed system logs
questions.explanation: Internet port-mappers and automated crawlers log exposures instantly whenever private internal resources are inadvertently given public network pathways or open firewalls.

questions.question: Why might a sudden spike in network traffic combined with high CPU usage be an early indicator of a cyberattack?
options: A cryptominer or DDoS operation is consuming system resources
A scheduled patch deployment is running longer than expected
A system update temporarily shut down the firewall
A user accidentally triggered a backup during peak hours
questions.explanation: Concurrent maximum spikes across both network connections and compute layers signal potential exploits, reflecting either DDoS flooding overhead or illicit background cryptomining processes.
